# DPFT: A blockchain-enabled differentially private federated transformer for trust evaluation in vehicular networks
Wajahat Ali, Fahd Raza, Arshad Iqbal et al. · AIMS Mathematics 2026 · https://doi.org/10.3934/math.20261146 · relevance: medium · basis: abstract

**Problem:** Intelligent transportation systems (ITS) rely on distributed data generated by connected vehicles, roadside infrastructure, and edge sensors.
**Approach:** This study proposes a differentially private federated transformer (DPFT) framework for privacy-preserving node trust classification in vehicular networks.
**Tools and scale:** The blockchain component processes 55 transactions per second with a latency of 248 milliseconds, demonstrating practical scalability under the evaluated federated simulation setting.
**Results:** Experimental results show that DPFT achieves an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.90, an F1 score of 0.77, and more than 78% classification accuracy. It outperforms FedAvg-long short-term memory (LSTM) and FedAvg-Trans and maintains over 70% accuracy when 25% of the participating nodes are Byzantine.
**Limitations and future work (as stated by the authors):**
- None stated in the abstract.
**Overlap with our engine:** partial — addresses security overhead or cryptography (direction 2 area); pseudonym privacy/linkability (runner-up area), but per the abstract without an integrated SCMS backend, closed-loop revocation, per-message joint ground truth or counterfactual reruns.
**Novelty implications:** Does not rule out any candidate direction on the evidence of the abstract. Leaves open quantifying this in a closed loop with real SCMS revocation and traffic safety outcomes.
